content.title: Getting back to flow in human–agent teams
content.tagline: A library of where flow gets stuck in human–agent teams, why, and what to try.

definitions.edge: Carries work between nodes. Has bandwidth.
definitions.sink: Where value lands: customers and the business.
definitions.output: The work moving along the edges.

content.key_line: Output is the work moving along the edges. Flow is what reaches the sink.

lenses.process: How work moves, norms, rituals, decision rights

worked_example.title: Example: review backs up at Ana and Ben (A1)
worked_example.setup: A PM sends PRDs to two engineers, Ana and Ben. Each directs three agents. The agents open about 30 PRs a week, and Ana and Ben review all of them. Output is up; customers get about as many working features as before.
worked_example.root_cause: The human ↔ agent edge sends more PRs than two people can review.

fixes.process: Agents review agent PRs; humans review only what gets escalated
fixes.tech: An automated check that escalates risky PRs to a human

practices.title: Every agent ↔ agent edge needs a human who can see it
points: What checks it, other than another agent?
practices.example: A coding agent opens a PR, an AI reviewer approves it, and CI runs tests the coding agent also wrote.

practices.title: Incidents are where people now learn what the network is doing
points: Track incidents and link them to the changes behind them
practices.example: A clear severity taxonomy makes trends comparable. Escaped defect rate shows, of everything shipped, how much was wrong.

stuck_points.name: Review backs up
stuck_points.symptom: Review queues grow and approvals turn into “LGTM”

root_causes.text: More output arriving than reviewers can judge

remediations.text: Agree as a team which changes truly need a human reviewer
PR size limits
Risk-tiered review: agents review agent PRs, humans review what gets escalated
Automated check that escalates risky PRs to a human

root_causes.text: Too few people trusted to review

remediations.text: Grow more reviewers
Pair juniors on reviews
Rotate review duty
Code owners that spread review across more people

root_causes.text: Reviewers spend time on mechanical issues

remediations.text: Agree what humans review for: intent, design, risk
Settle style rules once, not in every review
AI pre-review for style and obvious defects
Linters and formatters in CI

stuck_points.name: Context is stuck with one person
stuck_points.symptom: Work waits; agents and humans act on partial information
signals: Time for a new person to make a standard change

remediations.text: Recognize documentation as real work
Decision records
Documentation as part of done
Searchable docs kept next to the code
Rotation
Pairing with the context holder
At least two people per area
Code owners list at least two people
Name an owner for each agent's context
Update agent context files when decisions change
Repo-level context and rule files

stuck_points.name: Decisions stall
stuck_points.symptom: Approvals pile up at a leader

remediations.text: Name a decider for each type of decision
Decision-rights map
Reversible vs. irreversible tiers
Decision log

root_causes.text: Judgment not grown below the leader

remediations.text: Delegate with coaching
Leader reviews outcomes, not every decision
Decision log that records the reasoning, so others can learn it

stuck_points.name: Capacity depletes
stuck_points.symptom: Burnout; output holds briefly, then collapses

root_causes.text: AI raised the pace bar with no recovery cycle

remediations.text: Reset expectations
Protect recovery time
Explicit no-go hours
Quiet hours for notifications and agent pings

root_causes.text: On-call and alert load are rising

remediations.text: Spread on-call fairly and recognize it
Sustainable rotations
Cut alert noise

stuck_points.name: Accountability blurs
stuck_points.symptom: People own agent output they don't understand
signals: Reverts of changes the author couldn't explain

remediations.text: Norm: the author can explain the change
PR template asks the author for the why and the risks
Link each PR to the spec or agent session it came from

root_causes.text: No ownership defined for AI-produced work

remediations.text: Leaders say plainly that humans own agent output
Explicit owner per change and per agent workflow
Required human-owner field on agent PRs

stuck_points.name: Judgment atrophies
stuck_points.symptom: People stop challenging agent output and struggle without it
signals: Issues humans catch that agents missed
Time to diagnose a problem without an agent

remediations.text: Protect time for solving problems unaided
Form your own view before seeing the agent's on selected tasks
Agents show alternatives, not a single answer

stuck_points.name: Output is plausible but wrong
stuck_points.symptom: Agent work looks right but isn't

remediations.text: Write specs that state intent and constraints
Definition of ready for agent tasks
Project context agents can read
Fund engineers to own coherence
Standing tech-debt allocation
Architecture checks agents must pass

stuck_points.name: Output doesn't match priorities
stuck_points.symptom: Work in progress multiplies
signals: Share of shipped work tied to a roadmap outcome

remediations.text: Engineers decide what each agent works on
Every agent task maps to a backlog item
Scope agents to backlog items
Leaders state priorities often
WIP limits that include agent work
One board that shows agent and human work together

stuck_points.name: Agent performance drifts
stuck_points.symptom: An agent that worked well starts producing worse results
signals: Success rate on a fixed set of sample tasks
Quality after model, prompt or tool changes

root_causes.text: Agent setup changes without regression testing

remediations.text: A named owner for each agent's performance
Test changes against an evaluation set before rollout
Automated regression evals and version tracking
Someone owns keeping agent context current
Review agent context when architecture or priorities change
Freshness checks on agent context

stuck_points.name: Agent economics are invisible
stuck_points.symptom: No one can tell whether agents create more value than they cost
signals: Human review time per agent change

root_causes.text: Teams count output, not the full cost of producing it

remediations.text: Leaders accountable for net value, not output
Count review and rework in the cost of agent work
Track agent spend alongside the human effort it creates

stuck_points.name: Handoffs lose context
stuck_points.symptom: Surprises at integration; cross-team rework
signals: Waiting on answers from other teams

remediations.text: Pair on cross-team pieces
Shared demos
Handoff rituals
Shared notes on tickets and PRs that humans and agents both update

root_causes.text: No visibility into each other's work

remediations.text: Name an owner for cross-team syncs
Short written weekly updates
Shared view of in-flight work

stuck_points.name: Problems surface late
stuck_points.symptom: Disagreement goes underground

root_causes.text: Low trust: hard to admit “I don't understand this”

remediations.text: Regular 1:1s
Leaders model saying it first
Blameless retros
Anonymous question channel
Leaders protect time for feedback
Restore retros and feedback with intent
Lightweight pulse survey

stuck_points.name: Dependencies are invisible
stuck_points.symptom: Work is blocked by dependencies nobody planned for
signals: Time blocked on other people or teams
Blocked work with no named dependency owner

remediations.text: Talk about dependencies early
Map dependencies during planning
Track dependencies across teams and agent workflows

root_causes.text: No one owns the interface between teams

remediations.text: Named owners for critical interfaces
Agreed response times for handoffs
Alerts when work waits longer than agreed

stuck_points.name: Delegation fails
stuck_points.symptom: Agent work rejected on the first pass

remediations.text: Treat spec-writing as a core skill
Definition of ready for agent tasks
Reusable task templates

stuck_points.name: Work bounces back and forth
stuck_points.symptom: Human and agent iterate without converging

remediations.text: Know when to stop delegating
Time-box before changing approach
Track which task types agents succeed at
Show agents examples of good work
Feed review comments back into agent context
Tests and examples instead of more prompting

stuck_points.name: Authority boundaries are unclear
stuck_points.symptom: Agents act beyond what was delegated, or humans own what they can't control
signals: Agent actions humans had to undo

root_causes.text: What agents may do on their own was never defined

remediations.text: Agree what agents can decide and do alone
Decision rights by risk and reversibility
Permission scopes, approval gates and action limits
The accountable person can step in at any point
Clear escalation and override steps
Pause, cancel and roll back agent workflows

stuck_points.name: Trust in agents isn't calibrated
stuck_points.symptom: People rubber-stamp agent work, or review everything the same way
signals: Acceptance rate of agent work by risk level
Defects missed in review of agent work
Review time vs. risk of the change

root_causes.text: People can't see where agents are reliable

remediations.text: Learn where agents succeed and fail
Review agent misses together in retros
Show provenance and track record next to agent output

stuck_points.name: Failures go unnoticed
stuck_points.symptom: Agent chains ship with nobody watching
signals: Agent workflows with a named owner
Agent workflows with an escalation path

remediations.text: A named human owner per pipeline
Review owned pipelines in regular ops reviews
Ownership metadata on every agent workflow
Decide where a human must look
Sample agent-only changes for human review
Independent verification
Run logs someone reads
Owner reachable for pipeline escalations
Escalation thresholds for low-confidence or high-risk work
Automatic escalation when checks fail or confidence is low

stuck_points.name: Agent handoffs break
stuck_points.symptom: One agent's output lacks what the next agent needs

root_causes.text: Agents assume different formats or inputs

remediations.text: An owner for each agent-to-agent interface
Handoff contracts that say what must be passed on
Shared schemas, validated at each handoff
Decide what context must survive each handoff
Handoffs include decisions made and open questions
Shared workflow state agents can read

stuck_points.name: Agents loop without progress
stuck_points.symptom: Agents retry, re-delegate or contradict each other without finishing
signals: Workflows running past their expected time

remediations.text: Define when an agent should stop and ask
Retry limits and escalation thresholds
Loop detection, budgets and timeouts

root_causes.text: Agents have conflicting goals or instructions

remediations.text: One owner for a workflow's priorities
Resolve conflicting instructions before agents run
Instructions managed in one place

stuck_points.name: Work piles up downstream
stuck_points.symptom: Testing, deploy or QA becomes the bottleneck

remediations.text: Shift capacity to the constraint
Small batches
WIP limits
Automate the constrained stage

stuck_points.name: The system stops learning
stuck_points.symptom: Incidents recur, defects escape, juniors stall

remediations.text: Leaders attend postmortems
Severity taxonomy (P0, P1, …)
Blameless postmortems
Incident tracker with follow-up items

root_causes.text: Juniors supervise agents instead of learning

remediations.text: Deliberate learning reps
Some junior-owned tasks done without agents
Agents set to explain their changes on learning tasks
Owner for each postmortem follow-up
Every postmortem names the change behind it
Incident tracking tied to changes

stuck_points.name: Effort goes to the wrong things
stuck_points.symptom: Activity is celebrated while outcomes stay flat
signals: Share of work tied to outcomes
What gets praised in reviews and all-hands

remediations.text: Recognize review, maintenance and impact
Impact-based performance criteria
Dashboards that lead with outcomes

stuck_points.name: The bottleneck keeps moving
stuck_points.symptom: Fixing one constraint creates another somewhere else
signals: Wait time per stage over time
Lead time before and after a change
Downstream work in progress after upstream fixes

root_causes.text: Fixes optimize one stage, not end-to-end flow

remediations.text: Someone owns the whole path from source to sink
Judge changes by total lead time, not one stage
End-to-end flow view that shows queues
Involve downstream owners before changing a workflow
Review system-wide effects after a change
Watch downstream queues and rework after rollout

stuck_points.name: Shipped, but nothing moves
stuck_points.symptom: Features ship and no metric changes

root_causes.text: No success metric defined before building

remediations.text: PM and engineering agree on the metric together
Define the metric up front
Post-release review
Dashboard per initiative
Bring engineers closer to outcomes
Engineers join customer calls or a support rotation
Share product analytics with engineers
Name an owner for instrumentation
Instrumentation in the definition of done
Instrument before launch

stuck_points.name: Output up, customer experience down
stuck_points.symptom: More ships, but customers hit more friction and bugs

root_causes.text: Speed traded for usability and reliability

remediations.text: Customer experience is part of engineering quality
Usability and reliability in release criteria
Monitor customer-facing errors and task success

root_causes.text: Teams can't see how changes land with customers

remediations.text: Bring support and customer teams into feedback loops
Review customer impact after each release
Link support signals and analytics to shipped changes

stuck_points.name: Value fades after launch
stuck_points.symptom: A feature lands well, then its value declines
signals: Long-term change in the target metric

remediations.text: An ongoing owner for each outcome
Review outcomes again months after launch
Track adoption and outcomes over time

root_causes.text: Tech debt from building fast wears the feature down

remediations.text: Engineers own what they shipped, not just what's new
Standing time to maintain what already shipped
Track code coherence and defects per feature over time
